title: How to Dehydrate Blueberries in the Oven
excerpt: Learn how to dehydrate Fresh Pick blueberries in your home oven to enjoy a sweet, concentrated, natural snack that lasts for weeks in your pantry.
imageAlt: Baking tray with dark blue, wrinkled dehydrated blueberries next to a glass jar.
steps: Wash the Fresh Pick blueberries well with cold water and gently pat them dry with a clean cloth or paper towel.

Boil the 4 cups of water in a small pot with the lemon juice. Dip the blueberries in for 30 seconds so the skin cracks slightly (this helps them lose moisture quickly) and immediately move them to a bowl of cold water to stop the cooking.
Preheat your oven to the lowest temperature possible, ideally between 80°C and 90°C (175°F to 195°F).
Drain and dry the fruit completely. Spread the blueberries in a single layer on a baking tray lined with baking paper, making sure they don’t overlap.

Place the tray in the oven for 3 to 3.5 hours (210 minutes). Open the oven door briefly every hour to let the built-up moisture escape. They are ready when they look wrinkled and dry but firm to the touch.
Remove the tray from the oven and let it cool completely at room temperature for 60 minutes before packing.
tips: Because Fresh Pick blueberries are grown in the cold mountains of Guasca with a natural sweetness of up to 15° Brix, you don’t need to add any sugar to get a delicious, very tasty dried fruit.
Store the dehydrated blueberries in an airtight glass jar, in a cool place without direct light. They will keep in perfect condition for up to a month to go with your nuts, oatmeal or salads.
